choices: Call `GetForProfile()` in each test's `SetUpOnMainThread()` to force creation
Pass `/*create=*/false` so the service is never created implicitly
Override `ServiceIsCreatedWithBrowserContext()` to return `true`
Create the service lazily from a static `NoDestructor` instead of the factory
explain: Features should be created eagerly with explicit lifetimes, not lazily on first use. Lazy creation gives tests and production different initialization orders, which makes bugs hard to reproduce.

choices: It's fine: running synchronously on a cache hit avoids a needless task hop
The cache hit should post the callback so it's always async
The network path should block until the fetch completes, so it's always sync
Callers should be documented to check the cache first and handle the sync case
explain: A given callback must run either always synchronously or always asynchronously. Mixing the two means callers can't reason about when it runs; post the cached result with `PostTask` instead.

choices: Cache `item` and `config` in members on first use to avoid repeated lookups
Wrap the body in a `base::AutoReset` guard so re-entrant calls are ignored
Look the values up once at startup and store them in a global struct
Take `const Item&` and `const Config&` as parameters
explain: Keep control flow localized: pass the state a function needs as parameters instead of querying non-local state mid-execution. `AutoReset` guards are a last resort for unavoidable re-entrancy, not a substitute.

prompt: Which of these PRs should a reviewer ask to include an `InteractiveBrowserTest` Critical User Journey test?
choices: A new toolbar button that opens a native Views bubble
A new toggle on `brave://settings` wired directly to a pref
A new tab helper that records page-load timings in the background
A new `KeyedService` that syncs data with a backend server
explain: Features that add or modify user-visible native (Views) UI need at least one CUJ test. Don't require one for WebUI pages, trivial pref-wired toggles, or non-UI code like services and tab helpers.

prompt:
A PR adds a new dialog and tests it like this:

```cpp
class MyDialogTest : public BrowserWithTestWindowTest {};
```

The production code now contains `if (!browser_view) return;` to make the test pass. What should the reviewer say?
choices: Fine, as long as the null check carries a comment saying it's for tests
Switch to `TestWithBrowserView` so `browser_view` is never null in the test
Keep the test, but move the null check into a test-only `#if` block
Use an `InteractiveBrowserTest` CUJ test instead
explain: `BrowserWithTestWindowTest` forces test-only `if (!browser_view)` checks into production code. UI features should be covered by an `InteractiveBrowserTest` CUJ test, or by tests with proper dependency injection.

choices: Use `GetActiveUserProfile()` so the result follows the focused window
Take the `FooService*` as a parameter from the caller
Null-check the profile and return `false` when none has been loaded yet
Turn it into a member of a singleton so the profile lookup is cached
explain: Free functions and static methods must not reach into non-global state like profiles or windows. Have the caller pass in the profile- or window-specific dependency.

prompt: A new tab-scoped `ReaderModeFeature` must be queried by the toolbar button code to decide whether to show itself for a given tab. How should the feature be owned and exposed?
choices: As a plain `unique_ptr` in `BraveTabFeatures`, with a getter on the tab
As a `WebContentsUserData` helper fetched via `FromWebContents()`
Via Unowned User Data, with a static `From(tab)` accessor
As a global `std::map<TabInterface*, Feature*>` owned by the button
explain: Self-contained tab/window features can be a plain `unique_ptr` member. When external code needs to retrieve the feature, use the Unowned User Data pattern with a static `From()`, separating lifetime from retrieval.

prompt: You need a browser test where every tab gets a `MyTabFeatureMock` instead of the real Unowned User Data feature. What's the recommended approach?
choices: Add a factory override for testing before the browser is created
Use `BrowserWithTestWindowTest` and attach the mock to its fake tab strip
After startup, delete each tab's real feature and construct the mock in its place
Add a `--use-mock-tab-feature` switch checked inside `BraveTabFeatures::Init()`
explain: For integration tests, install a factory override via `GetUserDataFactoryForTesting().AddOverrideForTesting()` before the browser starts. For unit tests, attach the feature directly to a mock interface's `UnownedUserDataHost`.

choices: `barrier` is copied into each fetch, so `done` runs once per item
With empty `items`, `done` never runs; handle that case first
`done` must be bound with `base::Unretained` before being passed in
`BarrierCallback` requires a fixed compile-time count, not a `size()`
explain: A `BarrierCallback` created with a count of zero never fires its done callback. Check for the empty case and run the callback (e.g. with `{}`) and return early.

prompt: Your PR adds two new P3A histograms reporting how often users open a new panel. Code review is approved and CI is green. What else must happen before merging?
choices: Nothing; P3A is already privacy-preserving, so new metrics need no extra review
Add the histograms to `histograms.xml` and get an OWNERS approval there
Ship them behind a feature flag off by default until data has been reviewed
Describe the metrics in the p3a Slack channel for privacy review
explain: New P3A metrics have strict privacy requirements. Post a brief description in the p3a Slack channel so the analytics team can do a privacy review before you merge.

prompt:
During review you notice a new persisted pref:

```cpp
inline constexpr char kShowSidbarButton[] =
    "brave.sidbar.show_button";
```

The feature is landing behind a flag. What's the right call?
choices: Leave it; the key can be renamed once the feature is enabled by default
Fix only the C++ constant name; the stored string never matters to users
Fix the key string now, before the first release ships it
Leave it and file a follow-up to add a migration in a later release
explain: Persisted pref keys must be spelled correctly before the first release that includes them. Changing a key after it ships requires a migration to avoid losing user data.

prompt: While implementing a new Wallet setting, you notice an unrelated crash in the Rewards panel and also want to reorder methods in a file you aren't otherwise touching. What should you do?
choices: Fix both in this PR so reviewers only need to load the context once
Fix the crash here since it's urgent; defer only the reordering
Include both, but mention each one clearly in the PR description
Put the crash fix in its own PR and skip the reordering
explain: Each PR should have a single main purpose. Unrelated bug fixes and aesthetic reordering are ride-along changes; they make review, reverts, and bisecting harder.

prompt:
A PR adds this to `components/playlist/core/common/DEPS`:

```
include_rules = [
  "+components/prefs",
]
```

so that `common/utils.h` can declare `bool IsPlaylistEnabled(PrefService* prefs);`. What should the reviewer say?
choices: Fine, since `PrefService` is a component rather than `//chrome` code
Move the helper into `core/browser/`, where prefs are valid
Forward-declare `PrefService` in the header instead of adding the DEPS rule
Keep it in `common/` but guard the declaration with `#if !BUILDFLAG(IS_IOS)`
explain: `common/` is compiled into every process that links the component, so it can't depend on browser-only APIs like `PrefService`, `Profile`, or `g_browser_process`. A new `+components/prefs` in a `common/DEPS` usually means the code belongs in `browser/`.

choices: Always build the service and have it check the pref at runtime
Move the pref check into the static `GetForProfile()` accessor
Check `base::FeatureList` as well, so both must be enabled
Observe the pref and call `BrowserContextShutdown()` when it flips
explain: A factory may return `nullptr` only on session-stable attributes: profile type, buildflags, or feature flags. Gating on a user-toggleable pref (in the builder or the accessor) forces a restart for the toggle to take effect.

choices: Keep `Browser*` but store it as `raw_ref<Browser>` so it can't be null
Fetch prefs from `ProfileManager::GetActiveUserProfile()` instead
Take `BrowserWindowInterface*` instead, since it's the modern replacement
Inject the `PrefService&` it actually uses via the constructor
explain: Features should take exactly the dependencies they need at construction. `Browser` is a god object and globals hide coupling; even a narrower lookup key is worse than injecting the specific resolved dependency.

choices: Move it to `AttachPrivacySensitiveTabHelpers()` so it skips incognito
Own a plain class as a `unique_ptr` in `BraveTabFeatures::Init()`
Keep it, but add the helper to the presubmit allowlist
Call `CreateForWebContents()` from `brave_tab_features.cc` instead
explain: Tab-scoped features are plain classes owned by `BraveTabFeatures` and created in `Init()`. `AttachTabHelpers()` is only for helpers that must also attach to non-tab `WebContents`.

choices: Nothing; a tab feature and its `WebContents` share the same lifetime
It should hold a `WeakPtr<WebContents>` so it can detect destruction
Discarding swaps the contents; use `ContentsObservingTabFeature`
Observers must be registered in `Init()`, not in the constructor
explain: On desktop, discarding a tab replaces its `WebContents`, so a cached observer or `WeakPtr` goes stale. Use `ContentsObservingTabFeature`, or hold the `TabInterface` and call `GetContents()` at the point of use.
